newsitem.title: CHINA: French firms in big gains in China aviation market.
newsitem.headline: French firms in big gains in China aviation market.

text.p: French industry took a major stride on Thursday to carve out a niche in China's rapidly expanding aviation industry, with sales of over $1.5 billion of aircraft and a foothold to manufacture a new jet.

European consortium Airbus Industrie signed a $1.5 billion deal with China Aviation Supplies Import and Export Corp in the presence of visiting French President Jacques Chirac in the Great Hall of the People to sell 10 A320 and 20 A321 jets to China airlines.

"This marks the penetration into China of the A321," Airbus president and managing director Jean Pierson told reporters. "Today's contract is an additional strong vote of confidence by our Chinese customers in the A320 family.
"It's a very important success and there will be other ones," he said, referring to future prospects for Airbus in China's rapidly growing aviation industry.
Airbus signed a previous deal to sell 30 A320 jets to China during a visit by Premier Li Peng to France last year.

Airbus airliners hold a 15 percent market share in China, but Chinese officials have said they plan to expand that to bring it closer to the level of Boeing, which currently dominates China's airways.
Delivery of the aircraft was scheduled for 1998 through 2000, with three A320s going to China Southern Airlines and another two to Sichuan Airlines in the southwest.
Airbus also joined Alenia Aerospazio Spa -- a unit of Italy's Finmeccanica -- Aviation Industries of China and Singapore Technologies Aerospace in signing a contract to manufacture a 100-seat jet.

The agreement brings Italy's Alenia into the consortium to produce the regional airliner, to be assembled in China, in an estimated $2.0 billion project expected to build about 1,000 jets. The new family of jets was set to enter service by 2003.
Airbus and Alenia together would hold a 39 percent stake, with Alenia holding about 38 percent of that. The Chinese side would hold 46 percent and the Singapore partner 15 percent.
The new aircraft family would initially produce two versions of 105 seats and 125 seats and hoped to capture a significant share of the world market, Airbus said.
AVIC signed an accord with French state-owned aerospace group SNECMA to cooperate on building engines for the 100-seater jet, company officials said.
Competition has been fierce to supply the engines for the regional airliner to be assembled in China.
AVIC signed a letter of intent with Blanc Aero, a subsidiary of GFI Industries, on aeronautics and a cooperation agreement with Eurocopter to develop 5.5 tonne rotors.
Alenia also signed an agreement to sell five ATR-72 turboprop aircraft to China's Xinjiang Airlines, based in the northwestern city of Xinjiang, with an option for another five.
The deal was valued at about $80 million, officials said.

AVIC signed an agreement with the Aero International (Regional) consortium that groups Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc and Alenia to produce rear fuselage sections of the ATR 72 turboprop at China's Xian Aircraft Company.
